report.title: Moonshot AI ships Kimi K2.7-Code open-weight coding model
report.summary: Kimi K2.7-Code landed June 12 on Hugging Face (Modified MIT) and the Moonshot API at $0.95/$4.00 per million tokens — OpenAI- and Anthropic-SDK compatible via a one-line base URL swap. Moonshot claims 30% fewer reasoning tokens and double-digit benchmark gains over K2.6, though all benchmarks are first-party; independent evals pending.

report.title: Anthropic splits Claude billing into chat and Agent SDK pools starting June 15
report.summary: Starting tomorrow, Anthropic separates subscription credits into two pools: one for chat and first-party tools, another for programmatic Agent SDK and Claude Code usage at $20/$100/$200 per tier. Heavy agent-framework users who don't opt into overflow billing at full API rates will hit hard limits — action required before EOD today.

report.title: OpenAI quietly updates GPT-5.5 Instant for better response style
report.summary: OpenAI pushed a silent update to GPT-5.5 Instant in ChatGPT and the API, targeting readability, conversational pacing, and fewer bullet-heavy outputs. No version bump or changelog entry — same model ID, changed behavior.

report.title: OpenAI deprecates GPT-4.5 and o3 from ChatGPT, sets retirement dates
report.summary: GPT-4.5 exits ChatGPT on June 27 (30-day sunset); o3 follows August 26 (90-day sunset). Both remain live on the API with no changes — ChatGPT-only cleanup to consolidate around the GPT-5.x line.

report.title: US government orders Anthropic to restrict Fable 5 and Mythos global access
report.summary: The US government directed Anthropic to shut down global access to Fable 5 and Mythos, citing alleged jailbreak risks. Anthropic is complying while publicly contesting the severity of the vulnerabilities — a significant policy flashpoint for builders in regulated markets.

report.title: Google ships Vector Search 2.0 GA on Vertex AI with auto-embeddings
report.summary: Vector Search 2.0 is now generally available on Vertex AI, adding collections that unify data and vectors alongside auto-embeddings that populate vector fields without manual pipeline work. Drop-in upgrade for RAG and retrieval-heavy apps already on GCP.

report.title: LM Studio launches Enterprise tier for local LLM deployments at scale
report.summary: LM Studio added an Enterprise tier targeting organizations running local models under privacy, compliance, or cost constraints — the first paid tier for a tool that has been free and developer-focused since launch. Signals local LLM tooling is crossing into formal IT procurement.

learn.name: GitHub Copilot Desktop App
learn.oneLineDescription: Agent-native desktop app for managing parallel Copilot sessions across repos.

detail.whatItDoes:
The GitHub Copilot desktop app is a native client for Windows, macOS, and Linux that treats AI agents as first-class, parallel workers. From a single 'My Work' view you can see active sessions, open issues, pull requests, and background automations across all connected repositories. Each agent session runs in its own git worktree so multiple agents can work concurrently without conflicting — you can then use 'agent merge' to bring changes together.

The app supports both cloud sandboxing (remote execution on GitHub infrastructure) and local sandboxing (process-isolated execution on your machine) with per-repo policy controls. It ships alongside the GitHub Copilot SDK, now GA in Node.js/TypeScript, Python, Go, .NET, Rust, and Java, letting you build custom tools the agents can call.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers who already use Claude Code or Codex CLI for multi-file tasks and want a GUI control plane. Useful for engineering managers who want visibility into what agents are doing across a team's repos. Requires an existing GitHub Copilot subscription (Pro, Pro+, Business, or Enterprise); Free users are on a waitlist.
pros: Parallel agent sessions in isolated git worktrees prevent conflicts with zero manual branching setup
Unified 'My Work' view across repos reduces context-switching when directing multiple long-running agents
GitHub Copilot SDK now GA in 6 languages — build custom tools agents can call without Python lock-in
Cloud and local sandboxing options with RBAC policy support for enterprise compliance
cons: Technical preview only — not feature-complete; some workflows still require CLI fallback
Requires a paid Copilot subscription; no free tier at launch and Free-user waitlist timeline is unspecified
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- GitHub account with Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business, or Enterprise subscription
- Windows 11, macOS 12+, or Linux (x64/arm64)
- Git 2.38+ installed

## Install

Download the installer from the GitHub Copilot app page:

```bash
# macOS: install via the downloaded .dmg, then verify
copilot --version

# Linux (Debian/Ubuntu): download .deb from the GitHub Copilot releases page
sudo dpkg -i github-copilot-app_*.deb
copilot --version
```

## Authenticate

```bash
# Launch the app and sign in via browser OAuth
copilot auth login
# Follow the browser prompt; your token is stored in the system keychain
```

## Connect a repository

```bash
cd ~/your-project
# The app auto-detects repos; open My Work to see it appear
copilot workspace connect .
```

## Start a parallel agent session

In the app UI:
1. Open **My Work** > **New Session**
2. Type a prompt or drag in a GitHub Issue
3. The agent spawns in an isolated git worktree under `.git/worktrees/`
4. Start a second session from the same view — both run concurrently

```bash
# Verify worktrees created by the app
git worktree list
```

## Gotcha
The app requires `git worktree` support, which means your repo must not be a bare clone and must be on git 2.38+. Shallow clones (`--depth 1`) will cause agent sessions to fail silently on file-history-dependent tasks.

learn.name: Google Antigravity CLI
learn.oneLineDescription: Go-based successor to Gemini CLI with async multi-agent workflows and MCP support.

detail.whatItDoes:
Antigravity CLI (invoked as agy) is Google's closed-source replacement for Gemini CLI, built in Go for lower latency and a smaller binary footprint. Unlike Gemini CLI — which exposed a single Gemini session in the terminal — Antigravity CLI is designed as one surface of the broader Antigravity agent platform. It can orchestrate multiple background agents for complex tasks (large-scale refactors, parallel research) without locking your terminal session, and shares the same agent harness as the Antigravity 2.0 desktop app.

Key capabilities carried over from Gemini CLI: Agent Skills, Hooks, Subagents, file operations, shell execution, Google Search grounding, MCP server integration, and persistent context via an AGENTS.md file (renamed from GEMINI.md). Extensions are now Antigravity plugins. Asynchronous workflows are new — you can fire off a task and get a notification when it completes rather than waiting at the prompt.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers who used Gemini CLI and need to migrate before June 18, 2026 (the hard shutoff date for free, Pro, and Ultra personal Gemini CLI access). Also relevant for any team running CI/CD pipelines that call the gemini command — those will break on June 18 with no grace period. Enterprise Code Assist Standard/Enterprise customers keep Gemini CLI access, so migration is not urgent for them.
pros: Ships as a single native Go binary — no Node.js or Python runtime required
Async background agents free the terminal for other work during long-running tasks
Existing Gemini CLI extensions migrate via agy plugin import gemini with one command
Unified backend with Antigravity desktop app means CLI improvements propagate automatically
cons: Closed-source — community cannot inspect or contribute code, unlike the Apache 2.0 Gemini CLI
Not feature-complete at launch relative to Gemini CLI; some advanced Skills and Hook patterns have no equivalent yet
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- macOS 12+ or Linux (x64/arm64); Windows support in preview
- Google Cloud project or Google AI Studio API key
- Existing Gemini CLI users: migrate before June 18, 2026

## Install

```bash
# macOS/Linux: install via the official installer
curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/install.sh | bash

# Verify
agy --version
```

## Authenticate

```bash
# Personal Google account (60 req/min free tier)
agy auth login

# Google Cloud project (Vertex AI)
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="your-project-id"
agy auth login --gcloud
```

## Migrate from Gemini CLI

```bash
# Import existing Gemini CLI extensions as Antigravity plugins
agy plugin import gemini

# Rename config file (Antigravity reads AGENTS.md, not GEMINI.md)
mv GEMINI.md AGENTS.md

# Move skills directory
mv .gemini/skills/ .agents/skills/

# Update any CI scripts
# Old: gemini -p "run tests"
# New:
agy run "run tests"
```

## Run your first task

```bash
cd your-project
agy "Refactor all usages of the deprecated Logger class to use StructuredLogger"
# Antigravity spawns background agents; your terminal stays free
agy status   # check progress
agy attach   # re-attach to see output
```

## Gotcha
The agy command is not available in PATH until you restart your shell or run `source ~/.bashrc` (or `~/.zshrc`). The install script appends to your shell profile but does not reload it. Also: GEMINI.md is NOT automatically read — you must rename it to AGENTS.md or Antigravity CLI will have no persistent context.

learn.name: OpenAI Codex CLI + Sites Plugin
learn.oneLineDescription: Terminal coding agent with new Sites plugin for deploying apps hosted by OpenAI.

detail.whatItDoes:
OpenAI Codex CLI is the open-source terminal agent (github.com/openai/codex) that runs GPT-5.5 or GPT-5.3-Codex models locally, handling file edits, shell commands, git workflows, and multi-step coding tasks. The June 2026 update adds three notable capabilities: (1) standalone web search in code mode — agents can call search directly from nested JavaScript tool calls and receive plaintext results; (2) the Sites plugin (preview), which lets Codex create, deploy, and manage web apps, dashboards, and games hosted by OpenAI's infrastructure directly from the CLI or app sidebar; and (3) richer MCP tool schema support, preserving oneOf/allOf in tool input schemas so complex MCP integrations no longer break.

The Sites plugin is available in the Codex app sidebar and by default in ChatGPT Business workspaces. Enterprise admins can gate it via RBAC. Deployed sites get a hosted URL and support environment variable/secret management from within Codex.
detail.whoItsFor: Engineers who use Codex CLI for agentic coding tasks and want to ship internal tools, dashboards, or prototypes without setting up separate hosting. Also useful for anyone integrating MCP servers with complex schemas that previously got mangled by Codex's schema compaction. Requires a ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, or Enterprise subscription for full model access; open-source CLI works with any OpenAI API key.
pros: Sites plugin closes the prototype-to-URL gap — ship a dashboard without leaving the terminal
Web search in code mode lets agents look up documentation or APIs mid-task without a separate tool call
Preserved oneOf/allOf in MCP schemas fixes a long-standing pain point for complex tool integrations
codex doctor now includes editor/pager environment details to speed up debugging local installs
cons: Sites is preview-only — no SLA, and hosted environment variables are managed via OpenAI infra (no bring-your-own-cloud)
GPT-5.5 model access requires a paid ChatGPT plan; the open-source CLI defaults to whichever model your API key has access to
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Node.js 20+ (check: `node --version`)
- OpenAI API key with access to GPT-5.5 or GPT-5.3-Codex
- macOS or Linux (Windows support via WSL2 or the native Codex app)

## Install

```bash
npm install -g @openai/codex

# Verify
codex --version
```

## Authenticate

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."

# Or for ChatGPT subscription users (recommended for higher rate limits):
codex auth login
# Follow the browser OAuth prompt
```

## Run your first task

```bash
cd your-project
codex "Add input validation to the createUser function and write a test for it"
# Codex reads your codebase, proposes a plan, then edits files and runs tests
```

## Use the Sites plugin (preview)

```bash
# Inside Codex app: open the sidebar and click Sites
# From CLI:
codex "Build a React dashboard showing our API usage stats from data.json, then deploy it"
# Codex generates the app and calls the Sites plugin automatically
# You get back a hosted URL: https://sites.openai.com/your-site-id
```

## Enable web search in code mode

```bash
# Web search is on by default in code mode; to test it:
codex "Find the latest breaking change in the Stripe API and update our payment module accordingly"
# Codex will call web search inline before editing files
```

## Gotcha
The `--dangerously-auto-approve-everything` flag is real and bypasses all confirmation prompts — never run it against a production codebase. For CI use cases, prefer `--approval-policy on-failure` which only pauses on error. Also: MCP server configs live in `~/.codex/mcp_servers.json`, not in the project directory — a common source of confusion when onboarding teammates.

learn.name: MAI-Thinking-1 on Azure AI Foundry
learn.oneLineDescription: Microsoft's first in-house reasoning model: 35B MoE, 256K context, 53% SWE-Bench Pro.

detail.whatItDoes:
MAI-Thinking-1 is Microsoft's first proprietary reasoning model, a 35B active parameter Mixture-of-Experts architecture with a 256K token context window. It scores 97% on AIME 2025 and 53% on SWE-Bench Pro — placing it alongside Claude Opus 4.6 on the coding benchmark — and was trained entirely on commercially licensed data with no model distillation, giving enterprise teams a clean IP lineage for production deployment.

The model is available on Azure AI Foundry and via Baseten. It sits in the medium-weight class (comparable to GPT-5.4 Thinking by price/capability) and is specifically tuned for reasoning-heavy SWE tasks. Microsoft projects up to 10x improvement in output tokens per dollar compared to GPT-5.5 when fine-tuned via Foundry's Frontier Tuning (private preview), making it a cost-optimization target for agent pipelines that currently route to frontier models.
detail.whoItsFor: Azure-based engineering teams building agentic coding or reasoning pipelines that need a mid-weight model with clean IP lineage and competitive SWE-Bench scores. Also relevant for enterprises using GitHub Copilot on token-based billing — MAI-Code-1-Flash (the sibling model tuned for VS Code) is priced below Claude Haiku 4.5 and auto-routes from the Copilot model picker.
pros: 53% SWE-Bench Pro matches Claude Opus 4.6 at medium-weight cost, not flagship pricing
Zero distillation and fully licensed training data — defensible IP chain for regulated industries
256K context window supports large codebase or document analysis without chunking
Projected 10x token-cost improvement over GPT-5.5 when fine-tuned via Foundry Frontier Tuning
cons: Frontier Tuning (the key cost-optimization feature) is still private preview — most teams can't access it yet
Only available on Azure AI Foundry and Baseten at launch; not on AWS Bedrock or Google Vertex
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Azure subscription with Azure AI Foundry access
- Azure CLI installed and authenticated (`az login`)
- Python 3.10+ or Node.js 20+

## Deploy MAI-Thinking-1 via Azure AI Foundry

```bash
# Install the Azure AI Foundry SDK
pip install azure-ai-foundry

# Authenticate
az login
az account set --subscription "<your-subscription-id>"
```

## Python: call MAI-Thinking-1

```python
from azure.ai.foundry import FoundryClient
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

client = FoundryClient(
    endpoint="https://<your-foundry-endpoint>.openai.azure.com/",
    credential=DefaultAzureCredential()
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="mai-thinking-1",  # exact model ID from your deployment
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "Refactor this Python function to be async and add error handling: def get_user(id): return db.query(id)"}
    ],
    max_tokens=4096
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
```

## Deploy via Azure CLI

```bash
# Create a Foundry project (if you don't have one)
az ai foundry project create \
  --name my-mai-project \
  --resource-group my-rg \
  --location eastus

# Deploy MAI-Thinking-1
az ai foundry deployment create \
  --project-name my-mai-project \
  --model-id mai-thinking-1 \
  --deployment-name mai-thinking-prod \
  --sku Standard
```

## Enable in GitHub Copilot (MAI-Code-1-Flash)

```jsonc
// .vscode/settings.json — set Copilot to auto-route (may select MAI-Code-1-Flash)
{
  "github.copilot.chat.localeOverride": "en",
  "github.copilot.advanced": {
    "model": "auto"  // lets Copilot pick MAI-Code-1-Flash for cost-optimized tasks
  }
}
```

## Gotcha
MAI-Thinking-1 is billed per output token with a thinking-token surcharge (similar to o3/GPT-5.4 Thinking). If you're running batch eval jobs, set `budget_tokens` in the request to cap thinking depth and prevent runaway costs. The Foundry SDK exposes this as `reasoning_effort: "low" | "medium" | "high"`.

learn.name: OpenClaw (open-source local AI agent)
learn.oneLineDescription: Local-first AI assistant gateway to 50+ integrations with self-extending skill system.

detail.whatItDoes:
OpenClaw is an open-source personal AI agent that runs entirely on your own hardware, acting as a local gateway that connects AI models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, local Ollama models) to over 50 integrations including WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Signal, and iMessage. The agent is always-on — it can browse the web, fill forms, run shell commands, write and execute code, and control desktop applications. A standout feature is that it can write its own new skills, extending its own capabilities at runtime without manual intervention.

Originally created by PSPDFKit founder Peter Steinberger and open-sourced in early 2026, the project crossed 210,000 GitHub stars. In February 2026, Steinberger joined OpenAI and the project transitioned to an open-source foundation. Microsoft demonstrated OpenClaw running on the Surface Laptop Ultra at Build 2026, positioning it as the reference stack for always-on local agent workflows. The MXC sandboxing model used by OpenClaw is the same model adopted by GitHub Copilot CLI for process isolation.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers and power users who want an always-on local agent that bridges messaging platforms and desktop automation without routing data through a cloud assistant. Particularly useful for anyone building custom automations that span multiple communication channels. Security-conscious builders should review the broad permissions the agent requires — the skill repository currently lacks rigorous vetting for malicious submissions.
pros: Data never leaves your machine — all model calls go through local config, no cloud proxy required
50+ native integrations including iMessage, Signal, and WhatsApp without webhooks or third-party bridges
Self-extending: the agent writes new skills at runtime, so capabilities grow with use
210K+ GitHub stars and active community; MXC sandboxing model shared with GitHub Copilot CLI
cons: Requires broad system permissions (contacts, messages, file system, browser) — significant attack surface if a malicious skill is installed from the community repository
Skill repository lacks rigorous vetting; always review skill source before installing from the community hub
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- macOS 13+ (primary platform; Linux support is experimental, Windows via WSL2)
- Node.js 20+ and npm
- At least one API key: Anthropic, OpenAI, or a local Ollama instance
- For messaging integrations: the relevant app must be installed and accessible on your machine

## Install

```bash
npm install -g openclaw

# Verify
openclaw --version
```

## Initial setup

```bash
openclaw init
# Interactive setup wizard: sets your default model provider and API key
# Config is stored in ~/.openclaw/config.json
```

## Configure an AI model

```bash
# Anthropic Claude (recommended for coding tasks)
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
openclaw config set model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4

# Or use a local Ollama model (no API key required)
# First: brew install ollama && ollama pull llama3.2
openclaw config set model ollama/llama3.2
```

## Connect messaging integrations

```bash
# List available integrations
openclaw integrations list

# Connect Slack (OAuth flow)
openclaw integrations connect slack

# Connect iMessage (requires macOS with Messages.app signed in)
openclaw integrations connect imessage
# Grant Full Disk Access to the openclaw process in System Settings > Privacy
```

## Install a skill

```bash
# Browse community skills
openclaw skills search "github"

# Install a specific skill (ALWAYS review source before installing)
openclaw skills install openclaw-hub/github-pr-reviewer

# List installed skills
openclaw skills list
```

## Run the agent

```bash
# Start the always-on daemon
openclaw start --daemon

# Check status
openclaw status

# Send a test message in any connected channel:
# "@openclaw summarize my GitHub notifications from the last 24 hours"
```

## Gotcha
The most common setup failure is missing Full Disk Access permission on macOS, which silently prevents iMessage and file-system integrations from working. Go to **System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access** and add the `openclaw` binary. Also: the daemon writes logs to `~/.openclaw/logs/`; tail that file first when debugging integration failures.
